To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the volume of exhaled breath can be increased by increasing the tidal volume or minute ventilation, without changing the pH or nitrite concentration of the sample.

the volume of breath condensate collected can be manipulated by changing the target minute ventilation (7.5-22.5 L/min), tidal volume (500-1500 mL) and inspired air conditions (standard v cooler/drier).
the condensate volume is dependent on breathing pattern and the inspired air conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of breathing pattern (tidal volume and minute ventilation) and inspired air conditions (temperature and humidity) on the volume and composition of breath condensate.
the development of a new device for the collection of breath condensate.
the effect of the inspired gas conditions, the breathing pattern and the condenser design on the volume and composition of EBC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the volume of breath condensate can be increased by increasing Vm and Vt and that the volume of TEW can be increased by lowering Vt.
the condenser efficiency is 40% at Vm=7.5 l/minute, and it reduces to 29% as the minute ventilation is increased to 22.5l/minute.
EBC is a useful tool for noninvasive sampling of airway fluids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
condenser efficiency is reduced by high minute ventilation and low tidal volume, but that condenser efficiency can be improved by using a condenser with a large condensation surface area.
the volume of exhaled breath is a function of the minute ventilation, and the tidal volume.
the condenser used in this study is not efficient at higher Vm and that condenser efficiency is reduced at higher Vm, but not at higher Vt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
condensate collection should be performed with a high Vm and a high Vt.
EBC volume can be increased without compromising the dilutions of the samples.
the EBC pH, nitrite concentration and protein concentration are not influenced by changes in breathing pattern.
